scope: Frozen R125 Oracle daemon flat self-PC profile; eight event objects on one listener connection.

workload.listener_semantics: Eight ubus_event_handler objects registered on the same listener ubus_context; not eight independent clients.
workload.held_client_semantics: Additional idle libubus connections, independently validated with lookup.
workload.payload: One blobmsg u32 named value, equal to 0x12345678.
workload.loop: One send then synchronous pumping of the listener until all eight callbacks, before the next send.

limitations: Flat emitted-code samples do not identify inline callees or call counts.
Kernel function names are perf-reported, not validated by the user-ELF symbolizer.
C shared libraries provide dynamic exports only; hidden code and unmatched ranges remain unknown.
Raw sample counts/fractions and clocks under sampling are diagnostic, not router performance.
Daemon-only sampling cannot attribute caller CPU overhead.
Two reverse-order blocks per scale do not establish statistical superiority or causal attribution.
Eight receivers share one libubus connection; this does not characterize eight separate listener clients.
User sample resolution is 703/703 for R124 and 474/1074 for C. C has 455 libc and 145 libubox unknown samples.
R124 has only 166-180 user samples per window; small symbol differences are noisy.
Client HashMap::get_mut self-PC share is not all hash-table work and is not an optimization benefit ceiling.
No PC in a named allocator symbol does not establish zero allocations.
Daemon sampling cannot explain caller CPU differences or the prior physical-router wall-time outlier.
Sample totals and their ratios are not AX3000T performance ratios, statistical superiority, or causal effects.
No runtime change, new sampling, deployment, or final version-selection decision follows from this report.
